output.summary: Fast-growing leafy perennial shrub native to Mexico and believed to have originated from the Yucatán Peninsula through Central America to Panama. Damaged plants release irritating, often toxic latex, and some varieties have stinging hairs. Young leaves and tender stem tips are eaten cooked, but raw leaves contain toxic cyanogenic compounds, so thorough cooking is essential.
output.edibilityNote: Young leaves and tender stem tips are eaten boiled, steamed or stir-fried; raw leaves are toxic, and thorough cooking is essential.
